subject: Pathology
stem: An epithelial lesion has severe cytologic atypia but remains above an intact basement membrane. Which finding would establish local stromal invasion?

options.text: Malignant cells crossing the basement membrane
options.explanation: Penetration into the underlying stroma defines local invasive carcinoma.

options.text: Larger nuclei confined to the epithelium
options.explanation: Cytologic atypia alone can occur in carcinoma in situ.

options.text: More epithelial mitoses without stromal entry
options.explanation: Increased proliferation does not itself demonstrate basement membrane breach.
Pigment intensity does not establish malignant stromal penetration.

explanation: Carcinoma in situ has malignant epithelial cytology without penetration through the basement membrane. Stromal entry establishes invasion and changes access to the surrounding microenvironment and potentially lymphovascular channels. Atypia or mitotic activity alone does not prove this transition.
objective: Use basement membrane breach to distinguish invasive from in situ carcinoma.
